A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and relocation of technical material.

before.justification: v1 reports original closed-loop driving evaluations, training ablations, baseline comparisons, and qualitative outcomes in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds TransFuser results and a real-world versus 3DGS behavioral consistency analysis.

M1.justification: The policy architecture, discrete action space, three-stage training, rewards, PPO optimization, and auxiliary objectives are retained. The new reconstruction and buffer descriptions document previously unspecified implementation details; they do not establish a version-to-version change in the procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.4 adds evaluation of the same driving policy in a real-world environment alongside its 3DGS counterpart. The existing demonstration data and simulation benchmark remain; the rewritten description of scene diversity does not establish a different dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds TransFuser to the evaluated comparator set. VAD, GenAD, and VADv2 remain, with unchanged reported results.

E3.justification: The new consistency analysis introduces a same-policy comparison across real and reconstructed environments using temporal position traces. The existing 3968/337 training/evaluation split, nine benchmark metrics, and shared training settings remain unchanged. Newly specified clip duration, frame rate, and buffer mechanics are implementation disclosures.

E4.justification: v2 adds a simulation-to-real consistency case study. Conversely, Table 1 drops the 2:1 and 8:1 RL-to-IL sensitivity settings, and the illustrated unprotected-left-turn comparison disappears. Reward and auxiliary-objective ablations and the four appendix driving cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new trajectory plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, including RAD's collision ratio of 0.089. v2 adds TransFuser results, including collision ratio 0.320, and closely aligned real/simulated position traces. It removes the 2:1 and 8:1 ratio results, whose collision ratios were 0.137 and 0.125, and the left-turn qualitative example.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is retained. GAE, PPO clipping, and auxiliary-objective equations move from the main text into Appendices A.3–A.4; the combined objective is equivalently rewritten. Action definitions, imitation loss, dynamics, and metric formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first 3DGS-based RL framework for end-to-end driving, complementary benefits from combining RL and IL, and approximately threefold lower collision rates than IL baselines. The revised conclusion reiterates benefits already claimed or demonstrated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new consistency case as evidence that 3DGS evaluation reflects real-world driving performance. It removes non-reactive traffic from the explicit limitations, while Section 3.3 retains log-replay operation and newly discusses possible smart-agent and IDM alternatives.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation of environment construction and training execution. Appendix A.1 describes StreetGaussian extensions involving road meshes, separate sky modeling, object-pose optimization, and depth/normal supervision. Appendix A.5 adds 8-second, 10-Hz clips, 320-iteration RL rounds, and a four-clip FIFO buffer. Tables 5–6 disclose 128/32 RTX4090 GPUs, and the abstract adds an explicit code-repository pointer.

R1.justification: A new related-work paragraph distinguishes sequential and joint IL/RL approaches, adding CADRE, CIRL, and Huang et al. and expanding discussion of the already cited Lu et al. The broader positioning around photorealistic 3DGS training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: detailed optimization and auxiliary-loss material moves into dedicated appendix sections, main-text explanations are condensed, related work is rewritten, and the ratio-analysis narrative becomes a training-strategy comparison. The appendix structure is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column layout. Figures 3–4 are rearranged horizontally, a new consistency figure is inserted, the main qualitative figure loses its left-turn panels, and comparison and configuration tables are resized and restructured. The appendix qualitative montage is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through substantial reconstruction and training documentation, clearer related-work positioning, an additional baseline, and a direct real/simulated consistency case. These gains are limited by unchanged core results and the narrow validation example. Removing ratio-sensitivity results and the explicit non-reactive-traffic limitation weakens supporting evidence and qualification, but the improved documentation and added comparisons provide a modest net benefit.
